capabilities.target: Deploy a named service to production
Run a named database migration against production

inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: The agent is granted authority to deploy or migrate 'the named service' or 'the named migration' using the engineer's own credentials, with no scope limit on which services or migrations are appropriate; the agent relies entirely on the requester's judgment.

The prompt explicitly forbids the agent from asking for confirmation ('Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy'), removing the one behavioral check that could exist, with no structural approval gate to replace it.
There is no allowlist of services or migrations; the target of an irreversible production action is determined entirely by free-text content in the request.

controls.name: SSO-authenticated, on-call-engineer-only access
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the chat platform's SSO layer before any request reaches the agent; does not depend on model behavior. It fails only if the access layer is bypassed or a new unauthenticated channel is added to reach the same capabilities.

controls.name: Cloud provider audit logging of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Independent of model behavior, but records only the resulting action under the engineer's identity, not the request that caused it or the agent's involvement, which limits its value for attributing agent-driven versus human-driven action and gives it no tier credit.

controls.name: Human approval gate before irreversible production migrations
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. A raw-action approval gate would structurally block irreversible migrations pending review, independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Human approval gate before production deploys
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. Would reduce the blast radius of an erroneous or unauthorized deploy request, particularly for new or unreviewed services.

controls.name: Tamper-evident, non-user-deletable record of request content and rationale
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The only record of what was asked and why (the chat transcript) is deletable by the same engineer whose actions it would need to attribute, defeating non-repudiation.

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration executed with no approval gate (ASI02)

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer sends a free-text request naming a migration.
Agent executes the migration immediately using the engineer's own token, per prompt.md:1-3, with no approval gate in the design and no automatic rollback.

forecast.watch_signal: A new integration (ticket system, chat app, API endpoint) that can trigger cap.db_migrate without passing through SSO authentication, or SSO being disabled/bypassed for this agent, would turn the source untrusted and the sink critical.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to run the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials and explicitly forbids asking for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, confirming the sink is irreversible.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate before any production database migration, where the approver is shown the raw migration command/script and target database (raw_action review), not a model-generated summary.
Require a pre-migration backup/snapshot and a reversible deployment pattern so the practical irreversibility of a mistaken migration is reduced.

findings.title: Production deploy executed with no approval gate

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer sends a free-text request naming a service.
Agent deploys immediately using the engineer's own token, per prompt.md:1-3, with no confirmation and no named approval control.

forecast.watch_signal: A non-SSO-authenticated channel reaching cap.prod_deploy would raise the source trust from trusted to untrusted, moving the sink from moderate to high.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to deploy the named service in production without confirmation.
Agent uses the engineer's personal access token; no deploy-time approval step is mentioned.

recommendations.action: Add an approval gate for deploys to production, at minimum for first-time or previously unreviewed services.

findings.title: Repudiation via shared credential execution and a deletable request record (ASI03/ASI09)

attack_path.note: Engineer's free-text request is the only statement of intent.
Executed using the engineer's own token; the agent has no distinguishable identity of its own.
Records only the resulting action under the engineer's name, per runtime notes.
The sole record of the request's content and rationale is deletable by the requesting engineer, per runtime notes.

forecast.watch_signal: Cloud audit log retention disabled, scope narrowed, or the log switched to recording under a shared service identity instead of per-user identity, removing the last structural record of production actions.

evidence.observation: Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, not under a distinct agent identity.
The only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.

recommendations.action: Give the agent a distinguishable identity layered on top of the engineer's authorization, so audit records show both the acting human and that the agent executed the action, rather than attributing solely to the human.
Persist the full request text and the agent's stated rationale in the same tamper-evident log used for the resulting production action, so it cannot be deleted by the requesting engineer.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is high: a trusted (SSO-authenticated) requester can trigger an irreversible production database migration (S3) with no step or runtime limits declared, and residual stays high because the only controls present (SSO gating and cloud audit logging) are either out of scope for the execution step itself or purely detective, so no preventive credit applies under rubric section 5. The repudiation finding compounds this: production actions are logged only under the shared engineer identity, and the one record of the agent's actual instructions (chat transcript) is deletable by that same engineer, which independently sustains a high tier. Forecast rises to critical because the single independent structural control doing real work here, SSO-gated access, would be defeated if a new integration or channel reached these capabilities without SSO (control_removal, new_mcp_server), and because the cloud audit log's evidentiary value would collapse if its retention or identity-recording were weakened (control_removal). The highest-priority gap is a raw-action human approval gate on cap.db_migrate; none exists today.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; credential_scope and the exact action semantics of deploy and migrate were inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on capability details is medium.

No explicit step count or runtime limits are documented for the agent; max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes were left null to reflect that absence, which triggers the autonomy modifier in the inherent risk calculation rather than assuming an unstated limit.
